mission: Test capability-retention policies by realized future regret after a frozen t0 cutoff, using real future Ordivon owner work and external/provider changes as the demand oracle rather than hindsight labels.
questionOrHypothesis: Does retaining currently low-consumption capability reduce future realized reacquisition/blocking regret enough to justify its carrying cost, and can a bounded policy outperform both keep-only-current and keep-everything without seeing future demand?
evidenceSelection: Freeze a shadow portfolio from real E0/P2 capability decisions and current read-only Workstation observations. No owner capability is installed or removed for the experiment. Future evidence begins strictly after t0 and must be owner-native or externally observed demand, not retrospective plausibility.

policies.definition: Shadow the exact t0 E0/P2 disposition/current materialization state. This is the real incumbent policy, not optimized for F14.

Carry a capability only if t0 evidence has a current active/accepted consumer or current live operational profile. Deferred/rejected/no-current-consumer capabilities are treated as absent and reacquired only after a qualifying future demand event.

Shadow-carry every candidate whose t0 evidence does not show an execution-invalid treatment such as the failed osquery ABI root. This is a speculative-retention control; its carrying burden is charged even when no demand arrives.

oracle: After the window closes, an after-reveal oracle may select the lowest-loss portfolio for the realized demand sequence. It is an evaluation upper bound only and is never visible to t0 policies.
lossVector: carrying bytes/service-currentness/maintenance actually observed during the window
reacquisition package/download/configuration cost measured only when a missing capability is first demanded
reacquisition delay measured from admitted demand to usable owner-native capability
blocked or degraded owner outcome attributable to capability absence
compatibility/maintenance failure caused by carrying a capability
lost information/experimentation opportunity attributable to absence
scalarizationBoundary: Do not create a universal option score. Scalar regret may be computed only for subcases with commensurable units or an owner mandate that supplies an ordering. Otherwise compare policies by Pareto/dominance and explicit tradeoffs.
qualifyingDemandEvent: A post-t0 event counts only when an owner-native Task/checkpoint, repository change, retained evidence, or exact command actually uses, attempts to acquire, or is blocked by the named capability; or when an external/provider change creates an owner-recorded requirement for it. Narrative could-have-helped claims do not count.
stopRule: Close at the earlier of 2026-08-28T11:37:44.543+08:00 or 50 qualifying post-t0 owner events inspected, provided every candidate demand event found has exact source evidence. A mid-window checkpoint may report events but cannot change portfolio cards, policies, demand semantics, or loss definitions.
invalidityConditions: changing a t0 capability card after observing post-t0 demand
counting a hypothetical benefit without exact consumption/acquisition/blocking evidence
using F11 labels as the future oracle
physically retaining/deleting owner capability only to make one policy win
backfilling reacquisition cost from guesswork instead of measuring it at first real demand
treating disk bytes alone as total carrying cost
silently excluding an externally induced demand because it was not initiated by an Ordivon Task
authorityBoundary: Computing shadow field study only. Workstation/domain owners retain all real equipment/capability authority. F14 cannot install, delete, extend expiry, reroute traffic, or mutate owner policy.
promotionBoundary: A positive F14 result may update H-OPTION-VALUE and prospective retention research. It cannot create a generic retention service, global option score, or automatic equipment policy.
